newsitem.title: USA: Boeing sees 737 production at record by Q4.
newsitem.headline: Boeing sees 737 production at record by Q4.

text.p: Boeing Co said Thursday it plans to return production of its 737 aircraft to the previous all-time high of 21 planes per month by the fourth quarter of 1997, a level not seen since September 1992.
Boeing said it total orders currently stand at 645 airplanes valued at $47.26 billion, the second-highest dollar value in company history behind 1990's $47.7 billion.
The company will have a final 1996 order figure early next year.
Boeing said orders for its next-generation 737-600, -700 and -800 aircraft total 277 planes. Orders for 737-300, -400 and -500 models total 129 planes.
It said production of current- and next-generation planes currently runs at 8.5 per month.
Planned increases will take monthly 737 production to 10 airplanes in January, 12 in the second quarter, 17 in the third quarter, and 21 by the fourth quarter, it said.
Separately, Boeing confirmed an order from EVA Airways Corp for two 747-400 jetliners, valued at $330 million. Boeing will begin delivering the craft in 1997.
